extracted.intended_audience: potential grantees, partners, community organizations, philanthropy stakeholders, and the general public
extracted.subtask_description: High-level organizational principles and standards that guide RWJF's grantmaking, partnerships, evaluation, and stewardship, including commitments to health equity, evidence, transparency, and equitable philanthropic practice. Meant to orient prospective partners and the public to how RWJF operates and what it values in funded work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bold leaps, rooted in science and evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: “Bold leaps, rooted in science and evidence.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: RWJF describes its work as rooted in science and evidence and emphasizes that its actions and investments should be evidence-informed. The site signals use of multiple mechanisms (funding, convening, advocacy, evidence building, and impact investing) to pursue impact, implying preference for approaches grounded in scientific evidence and evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Health equity focus / address structural racism
rubrics_metrics.description: “...a commitment to address structural racism, a root cause of health inequities in the United States.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programs and investments should aim to advance health equity and explicitly confront structural racism as a root cause of disparities. RWJF frames its mission as creating “a more equitable society, centered in health and wellbeing,” so funded work should align with that aim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Work side-by-side with communities, practitioners, and institutions
rubrics_metrics.description: “Through funding, convening, advocacy, evidence building, and impact investing, we work side-by-side with communities, practitioners, and institutions to get to health equity, faster and together.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: RWJF values partnership and collaborative approaches: funded initiatives are expected to be developed and carried out in close partnership with affected communities, practitioners, and relevant institutions rather than being top-down.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency and accountability
rubrics_metrics.description: “We continue to push ourselves to be more transparent and accountable as we work to create a more equitable society.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The foundation commits to transparency and accountability in its operations and grantmaking. This extends to making financial disclosures available and being open about processes and impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equitable Philanthropic Practice
rubrics_metrics.description: “Equitable Philanthropic Practice — We are committed to learning and changing in our goal to tackling structural racism.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: RWJF expects its philanthropic practices to be equitable and to evolve. This includes ongoing learning, adapting grantmaking practices to reduce harm and advance equity, and centering equity in how grants are designed and administered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion (DEI) commitments
rubrics_metrics.description: “Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion — Explore our commitments.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The foundation explicitly lists DEI as a core commitment; applicants and partners should align with and demonstrate attention to DEI principles in programs and operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Learning and Evaluation / third-party research
rubrics_metrics.description: “We evaluate the impact of our funding and other actions through third-party research.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: RWJF prioritizes rigorous evaluation, including independent/third-party research to assess program impact. Proposals should anticipate and accommodate external evaluation and evidence-generation activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Good Stewardship / defined grant process and criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: “Good Stewardship — Who develops our grant programs? What criteria and objectives must be met? Learn about our grant process.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grant programs are developed according to defined stewardship processes and have explicit criteria and objectives that must be met. Prospective grantees should expect formal processes and stated objectives that guide funding decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial Transparency / disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: “Financial Transparency — Find our financial disclosures and additional information.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: RWJF publishes financial disclosures and expects financial openness; grantees and partners may be subject to financial reporting and disclosure requirements consistent with stewardship and transparency commitments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of multiple strategies to achieve impact
rubrics_metrics.description: “Through funding, convening, advocacy, evidence building, and impact investing...”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: RWJF employs a portfolio of strategies (direct funding, convening stakeholders, policy advocacy, building evidence, and impact investing). Strong proposals may leverage or align with one or more of these strategies rather than expecting grants alone to produce systemic change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Place-based / state-focused commitments (New Jersey and beyond)
rubrics_metrics.description: “New Jersey: Our Home State ... We are committed to improving health and advancing health equity for all in New Jersey and beyond.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The foundation maintains commitments to its home state while working nationally; applicants in New Jersey may find particular relevance or priority, though RWJF also supports broader, national work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for healthy, inclusive democracy as part of health
rubrics_metrics.description: “Answering the Call for a Healthy, Inclusive Democracy” (feature item) — During a time of calculated attacks against our democracy, we hear a call for justice from every neighborhood and community. A call for those with power, privilege, and resources to put those on the line for the betterment of everyone. And we will answer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: RWJF considers civic health and inclusive democracy relevant to health equity and may support work that defends or advances democratic participation and civic conditions as part of its health agenda.
